title: all_horizontal / any_horizontal are in the horizontal dispatch set but unimplemented in _eval_horizontal, always returning None
description: _HORIZONTAL_FUNCS (lines 114-123) includes 'all_horizontal' and 'any_horizontal', so _call routes them to _eval_horizontal (line 1733-1734). But _eval_horizontal only has branches for max_horizontal/min_horizontal/sum_horizontal/mean_horizontal/coalesce; all_horizontal and any_horizontal hit the final `return None`. Unlike the catalogued sum/mean/concat_str null-edge divergences, these are TOTALLY unimplemented — they return None for ALL inputs, not just edge cases, so the trace shows None where Polars returns a real boolean. The catalog's known horizontal finding enumerates only sum_horizontal(all-null), mean_horizontal(one-null), and concat_str; it does not mention all_horizontal/any_horizontal, and these route through the dispatch set rather than being merely unhandled functions. (Reported with low confidence as it may be considered subsumed by the broad 'horizontal funcs diverge' title.)
evidence: Executed repro (polars 1.39.2): out=pl.all_horizontal(pl.col('a'),pl.col('b')) with a=True,b=False -> evaluator result_value=None, real Polars=False. out=pl.any_horizontal(...) same inputs -> evaluator=None, real Polars=True. The function names are present in _HORIZONTAL_FUNCS so they reach _eval_horizontal, which has no matching arm and returns None at line 2017.
